title: Places in Town
description: Identify useful places and say where they are in town.
objectives: Identify useful places and say where they are in town.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to identify useful places and say where they are in town. The central language is place nouns and there is/are review. It belongs to the practical context of home & around town. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: place nouns and there is/are review

blocks.english: There is a pharmacy on Main Street.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the places in town exchange.

blocks.english: The bank is across from the park.
blocks.explanation: This places in town model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the places in town exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “There is a pharmacy on Main Street.” and “The bank is across from the park.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: place nouns and there is/are review.
